decisions.rationale: The span "breast and ovarian cancer" refers to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer) joined contiguously by "and", so it is a Composite Mention. It modifies "families", but the composite category captures the two-disease span.
decisions.guideline_section: 2. Annotate contiguous text strings; Examples 7 and 17

decisions.rationale: The span "breast / ovarian cancer" contiguously names two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer) and is used to describe families, so it is annotated as a Composite Mention rather than split into substrings.
decisions.guideline_section: 2. Annotate contiguous text strings; 5. Minimum necessary span of text

decisions.rationale: The span "breast and ovarian cancer" in the sentence about proportions of cases refers to two separate specific diseases in one contiguous string, making it a Composite Mention.

"ovarian cancer" names a single, specific disease mention (women having ovarian cancer) that can be linked to one definition without further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease. Cancer is retained as a disease term.
